Almighty God: Father, Son and Holy Ghost united in the Trinity
Christ in his humanity as our elder brother
The Father together with the Blessed Virgin Mary
why: When we say "Our Father" we address the one God in the adorable Trinity.

src.label: Baltimore Catechism Q. 5
src.quote: When we say "Our Father" in the Lord's Prayer we address Almighty God, Father, Son and Holy Ghost united in the adorable Trinity.
src.note: When we say "Our Father" we address the one God in the adorable Trinity.

q: According to the Baltimore Catechism, what do we ask for in "Thy kingdom come"?

That the world come soon to its final end
That all earthly rulers be cast down from power
That the Church may own more land and wealth
why: We ask that God reign in souls by grace for their salvation and that the true Church spread over the earth.

src.quote: we ask (1) that God may reign in the souls of all men by His grace

q: What does the word "daily" teach us in "our daily bread," according to the Baltimore Catechism?
o: To fast from bread on certain days of the week
To store up goods for the whole year ahead
To pray the Our Father only once each day
Great confidence in the providence of God
why: We say "daily" to teach us to be prudent, not avaricious, and to trust in God's providence.

src.label: Baltimore Catechism Q. 13
src.quote: We say "daily" to teach us that we are not to be avaricious but only prudent in providing for our wants; and that we are to have great confidence in the providence of God.
src.note: We say "daily" to teach us to be prudent, not avaricious, and to trust in God's providence.

q: What does the Baltimore Catechism say is the best means of overcoming temptation?
o: To argue with it at length
To seek it out and conquer it
why: Resist at the beginning, turn your attention away, pray for help, and do the opposite of what you are tempted to do.

src.label: Baltimore Catechism Q. 18
src.quote: The best means of overcoming temptation is to resist its very beginning
src.note: Resist at the beginning, turn your attention away, pray for help, and do the opposite of what you are tempted to do.

In memory of the Incarnation of Christ
In memory of the Nativity at Bethlehem

q: The Baltimore Catechism records a pious custom of saying the Sorrowful Mysteries on which days?
